summary: iter31: Tested new feature 'Repartition occupant/proprietaire' for decompte locataire annuel future. Backend: 13/13 pytest passed covering: (a) ExpenseCategory POST/PUT with default_occupant_pct + default_proprietaire_pct - 60/40 accepted, 70/40 (sum=110) rejected with 400 + 'doit etre 100' message, GET returns both fields, update persists, sum!=100 on update rejected; (b) Invoice POST with expense_category_id auto-inherits cat % (60->occupant_amount=60.0, proprietaire_amount=40.0 on total=100), explicit occupant_pct=20 override -> uses 20, proprietaire auto=80, occupant_amount=40 on total=200; (c) Invoice PUT without occupant_pct preserves existing value (25 stays 25), with new value updates; (d) Journal Entry OD: charge line on 612300 (with cat 60/40) auto-inherits 60/40, charge line on account WITHOUT cat defaults to 0%/100%, explicit occupant_pct=30 only (proprietaire_pct=None) auto-completes to 70 via _enrich_lines helper, both provided sum=80 (50+30) rejected with 400, PUT recalculates correctly. Frontend: Login as superadmin OK; ExpenseCategoriesPage create dialog shows cat-occupant-pct + cat-proprietaire-pct inputs, typing 60 in occupant auto-fills 40 in proprietaire (OK); InvoicesPage create dialog shows invoice-occupant-section + inv-occupant-pct + inv-proprietaire-pct, typing 30 in occupant auto-fills 70, 'Part occupant' live amount text present; JournalsPage OD new-entry dialog shows %Occ. + %Prop. column headers, and journal-line-{i}-occupant/proprio inputs are conditionally rendered ONLY when account_number starts with 6 or 7 (charge) - confirmed by code review (isCharge ternary at line 269/278 of JournalsPage.js) and matches the requirement 'Affichees uniquement quand account_number commence par 6 ou 7'.
critical_code_review_comments: ExpenseCategoryInput: validation 'sum=100' done BEFORE PCMN account check on POST. Good - rejects bad pct first. PUT also validates correctly.

InvoiceInput.occupant_pct/proprietaire_pct typed Optional[float]=None correctly distinguishes 'not provided' (inherit) from 'explicitly 0' (use 0). create_invoice: data.occupant_pct is not None -> use it; else inherit from category default; else 0%. update_invoice has correct 3-tier fallback: payload > existing > category > 0%.

Invoice create/update: proprietaire_pct is always RECALCULATED as 100-occupant (server-side ignores any client-provided proprietaire_pct value). This means client sending occupant=50 + proprietaire=30 silently becomes 50/50 - by design (single source of truth) but worth noting if frontend ever sends mismatched values.

_enrich_lines_with_occupant_pct: clean helper. Handles 3 cases: both None (inherit from cat if class 6/7, else None), one provided (auto-complete the other), both provided (validate sum=100). Correctly leaves non-charge lines (4xx/5xx) with occupant_pct=None.

_enrich_lines_with_occupant_pct minor edge case: if occupant_pct=100 with proprietaire_pct=None, occ+prop=100+0=100 so the if-branch is skipped and proprietaire_pct stays None. Not a bug but inconsistent: when occupant=0 alone, proprietaire stays None too. Future invariant 'sum=100 always' could be enforced by always auto-completing when one is None. Non-blocking for current scope.
ExpenseCategoriesPage / InvoicesPage / JournalsPage: all 3 implement two-way auto-complete client-side via setOccupant/setProprio with onChange. Math: +(100-v).toFixed(2). Clean.

JournalsPage: data-testid pattern 'journal-line-{i}-occupant' and '-proprio' is rendered only when isCharge=account_number starts with '6' or '7'. This matches the spec exactly. Non-charge lines show '—' span - clear UX.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all testids present, autocomplete working on cat + invoice, OD columns visible, conditional rendering verified)
